title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: Scripture sounding as if God created some unto contumely is to be read permissively — vessels of contumely by not adding special grace
pass_a_gloss: Finally, if any places of Scripture seem to sound unto this sense, as if God had created some unto contumely and perdition, they are, in my judgment at least, to be interpreted permissively. For he creates day by day those whom according to the decree of non-election or reprobation he permits to become vessels of contumely, by not applying that special grace which would make them vessels of honor.
pass_b_english: And last: wherever Scripture seems to speak as though God had fashioned some for disgrace and ruin, I judge those places to be taken permissively. Day by day he brings into being those whom, under the decree of non-election or of reprobation, he suffers to turn into vessels of contumely — withholding the special grace that would have made them vessels of honor.
source_text: Denique, si quae loca Scripturae in hunc sensum sonare videantur, quasi Deus creasset aliquos in contumeliam et perditionem, sunt, meo quidem judicio, interpretanda permissive. Creat enim indies, quos secundum decretum non-electionis seu reprobationis permittit fieri vasa contumeliae, non apponendo illam specialem gratiam quae faceret eos vasa honoris.
